readability.title: Energy Outlook
readability.full_text: The outlook for energy in two scenarios bp’s Energy Outlook 2025 uses two scenarios – Current Trajectory and Below 2° – to explore the speed and shape of the energy transition out to 2050 and to help shape a resilient strategy for bp. Current Trajectory is designed to capture the broad pathway along which the global energy system is currently travelling. Below 2° explores how different elements of the energy system might change in order to achieve a substantial reduction in carbon emissions. The global energy system The two scenarios are informed by recent trends and developments in the global energy system. In emerging trends , we discuss these recent developments across areas including energy demand, energy security, energy efficiency and carbon emissions. The scenarios can be used to help inform some key insights about how the energy system may evolve over the next 25 years. We discuss trends common across both scenarios, including strong growth in energy demand in emerging economies, rapid growth of wind and solar power, and the declining importance of fossil fuels. We also discuss trends that are more dependent on the speed of the transition, such as the pace of growth of modern bioenergy and low carbon hydrogen. We use the scenarios to explore the speed and shape of the energy transition out to 2050, then in the following pages discuss the outlook for the various energy types. Sensitivities We also explore the impact of other issues and uncertainties affecting the outlook of the energy system, by varying key aspects of Current Trajectory . Those issues include the risks of increased geopolitical fragmentation and of sustained weakness in energy efficiency gains.

readability.title: How Urban Trees Improve City Life
readability.full_text: Environment Trees are one of the simplest ways for a city to become cooler, healthier, and more pleasant. Although a single tree has a modest effect, thousands of trees distributed across streets and neighborhoods can change the character of an entire urban area. Cooling the streets Concrete and asphalt absorb solar energy during the day and release it slowly after sunset. Tree canopies interrupt this cycle by providing shade, while water released through leaves cools the surrounding air. The result can be a noticeable difference between a shaded street and an exposed parking lot. Improving public spaces People tend to spend more time outdoors when streets contain shade, greenery, and comfortable places to sit. Trees can therefore support walking, cycling, outdoor markets, and informal social activities. “A successful urban forest is not decoration. It is part of the city's basic infrastructure.” Planning for the future Planting trees is only the first step. Cities must also provide adequate soil, water, maintenance, and protection from construction work. Species should be selected according to local climate and the physical limits of each location. The most effective programs combine long-term maintenance with careful planning. When these conditions are met, urban trees can provide benefits for decades rather than for a single season.

September 12, 2026 · 08:45 AM · By Sarah Bennett The North Valley Observatory officially opened its new research center on Saturday, bringing together astronomers from six universities and several independent research groups. The facility contains a data center, laboratories, and offices for visiting scientists. Its primary purpose is to process observations collected by the observatory's new wide-field telescope. A larger view of the sky The telescope is designed to repeatedly photograph large sections of the night sky. Researchers hope this will allow them to identify objects that change brightness or position over relatively short periods. “The important thing is not just taking one picture,” said observatory director Helen Brooks. “We want to understand how the sky changes.” International collaboration Data from the center will be shared with research teams in several countries. Observatory officials said the project is intended to make astronomical data available to researchers who do not have access to large telescopes. The first public research results are expected to be released early next year.

readability.title: What I Learned From a Month Without Notifications
readability.full_text: September 10, 2026 · Alex Turner A month ago I turned off almost every notification on my phone. I expected the experiment to make me more productive, but the biggest change was surprisingly simple: I stopped feeling that I was constantly behind. The first few days were strange During the first week I repeatedly unlocked my phone without knowing why. The habit was so automatic that I sometimes checked the screen before remembering that there was nothing new to see. After several days, the behavior became less frequent. I began checking messages at specific times rather than responding whenever a small notification appeared. More uninterrupted time The most useful effect was not that I spent dramatically less time online. Instead, the time I spent working became less fragmented. Reading a document for twenty minutes without interruption felt much easier than it had before. The goal was never to use my phone less. It was to let me decide when the phone deserved my attention. Would I do it again? Yes. I still keep notifications enabled for calls and a few genuinely important services, but most applications remain silent. I now check them when I choose rather than when they choose for me. It is a small change, but it has made my days feel considerably calmer.

readability.title: Acme API Documentation - Authentication
readability.full_text: API REFERENCE / AUTHENTICATION Authentication The Acme API uses bearer tokens to authenticate requests. Every request to a protected endpoint must include a valid access token in the Authorization header. Creating an API key API keys can be created from the developer dashboard. Give each key a descriptive name so that it can be identified later. Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY Making an authenticated request The following example requests information about the current account: curl https://api.example.test/v1/account \ -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY" Response "id": "acct_12345", "name": "Example Account", "active": true Security recommendations Never commit API keys to source control. Store credentials in environment variables or a secret manager. Use separate keys for development and production. Rotate keys when they may have been exposed. Errors An invalid or missing token produces a 401 Unauthorized response. Expired tokens should be replaced before retrying the request.

readability.title: Example Encyclopedia - Solar Energy
readability.full_text: Solar energy Solar energy is energy derived from sunlight. It can be converted into electricity or used directly as heat. Solar energy is considered a renewable resource because sunlight is continually supplied by the Sun. Solar energy Type: Renewable energy Primary source: Sunlight Common technologies: Photovoltaics, solar thermal History Humans have used sunlight for heating and illumination for thousands of years. Modern solar technology developed through advances in materials science, electrical engineering, and manufacturing. Technology Photovoltaic cells convert light directly into electrical energy. Solar thermal systems instead capture heat from sunlight for uses such as hot water production or electricity generation. Switch preference is subjective, so trying a few types before buying is useful. layout_fan Member Don't underestimate layout. A compact board can save desk space, but removing dedicated navigation keys may be annoying if you write a lot. A standard tenkeyless layout is a good compromise for many people. old_timer Moderator Keycap quality matters mostly for feel and long-term wear. readability.title: The History of Public Libraries
readability.full_text: HISTORY From private collections to institutions designed to make knowledge available to entire communities. ADVERTISEMENT Learn a new language with our recommended courses. Public libraries are often described as places where people borrow books, but their history is much broader. They developed from a long tradition of collecting, organizing, preserving, and sharing written knowledge. Early collections were frequently controlled by governments, religious institutions, universities, or wealthy individuals. Access was limited, and books were expensive to produce. The modern idea of a publicly supported library emerged much later. From private collections to public institutions During the nineteenth century, changes in printing, education, urban development, and civic organization helped create demand for libraries that ordinary residents could use. In many cities, local governments and community organizations began establishing permanent collections. These institutions served several purposes. They provided access to books, supported education, created quiet places for study, and became community spaces where lectures and public meetings could take place. Libraries became important not because every visitor wanted the same book, but because communities benefited from having knowledge available in many forms. The changing role of librarians As collections grew, librarians developed systems for cataloging and organizing materials. Classification systems made it easier for visitors to discover books without already knowing what they wanted. Cataloging systems improved discoverability. Reading rooms provided dedicated spaces for study. Children's departments expanded access to younger readers. Reference services helped visitors locate specialized information. Weekly Knowledge Review Get our best articles every Sunday. Libraries in the digital age The arrival of computers and the internet changed libraries once again. Digital catalogs replaced many card systems, while electronic books and online databases expanded the range of resources available to visitors. However, the physical library did not disappear. Many libraries adapted by offering computers, internet access, meeting rooms, educational programs, and cultural events alongside traditional collections. What libraries provide today Service Traditional role Modern role Books Borrowing printed books Printed and electronic collections Research Reference books Databases and digital archives Community Reading rooms Events, workshops, and meeting spaces Technology Limited Computers, internet, and digital literacy programs Conclusion Public libraries have changed repeatedly as technology and society have changed. Their central purpose, however, has remained relatively stable: providing communities with access to information, learning, and shared cultural resources. The future library may contain fewer shelves than its predecessors, but it will continue to perform the broader work of connecting people with knowledge.
